text:
incident-bot: ⚠️ PAGER: Runtime queue backlog spiking in us-west-2. 95th latency > 6s for text-generation requests, error rate ~4.7% over last 5m. Affected model group: rwd-large-v1 variants. Paging on-call (priority: high).

maya: seeing the same in the dashboard, inflight is at 98% of max, queue depth ~4200. Some long-poll streaming requests are holding slots.

sam: confirmed. Traces show KV cache eviction thrash + a few very long seq requests (seq len > 8k) driving runtime GPU memory contended.

juan: tagging @olivia for customer impact — which customers routed here?

olivia: customers with dedicated routing remain fine. Hosted-tier noisy customers: corp-x and two unnamed PLG tenants. Corp-x showing ~15% of their requests failing 500s. Escalating to support to notify them.

maya: immediate mitigations I'm proposing: 1) apply short-term sheddings: cap max-inflight per-tenant to 60, 2) bump global token timeout from 120s -> 45s for streaming, 3) disable non-essential streaming features (delta-metrics) for 10m. Anyone object?

sam: +1 for caps. Can we also reduce per-request concurrent batch size to force shorter tail? current batch_size=16 -> set to 8.

juan: do we want to temporarily lower default model sequence max to 4k to avoid the ultra-long requests? Might cause truncation but prevents OOM.

maya: yes, do that for hosted group only. We'll keep Dedicated untouched. I'll make the config changes now.

maya: running commands now:
```bash
# set per-tenant inflight cap
redwoodctl runtime set-config --scope hosted --set 'max_inflight_per_tenant=60'
# reduce batch size
redwoodctl runtime set-config --scope hosted --set 'default_batch_size=8'
# lower streaming timeout
redwoodctl runtime set-config --scope hosted --set 'streaming_timeout_s=45'
# reduce max seq len
redwoodctl model set-config --models rwd-large-v1* --set 'max_sequence_length=4096'
```

sam: command outputs look good — 200 for each change. Applying admission policy to start shedding extra requests from noisy keys.

incident-bot: Action log: config changes deployed by maya at 3378912460. Health checks running.

olivia: support notified corp-x, they're switching heavy batch jobs to dedicated for the next hour. PR opened for customer-facing note.

sre_lead: good moves. I'm going to keep an eye on capacity and prepare to spin up a temporary extra GPU pool if latency doesn't drop in 5m. Also coordinate with infra for quick scale.

maya: after 3m, 95th latency down to 2.1s, queue depth 900, error rate down to 1.2%. Inflight at 64% now.

sam: observe a small uptick in tail errors for truncated streams (client side mis-handle), support to follow up. We should add a short message in the response body for truncated events so SDKs can surface it.

juan: agree — file a follow-up task to add explicit truncated flag and better 4xx vs 5xx classification.

maya: passing to next on-call. @sam you're on-deck, I'll set handoff. Current state: mitigations applied, system stable, customer impact reduced but corp-x still throttled.

sam: taking it. I'll monitor for 30m and coordinate with infra to scale if needed. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: incident closed for paging at 3378912945 (mitigations in place). Please update postmortem if follow-ups needed.
